source: User-pasted H200 CUPTI table and subsequent compiled_resources/comparison/paired_comparisons summaries
scope: GPU kernel durations, native resource counts, full/core API ratios, same-payload output check and paired trial summaries. Absolute API medians, raw paired trials and detailed validation cases were not supplied.
table_columns: attention, all kernels and all GPU work are equal for each reported row

jit_vs_candidate.note: Matched trial indices with randomized within-trial order; descriptive, not a significance test.
Matched trial indices with randomized within-trial order; descriptive, not a significance test.

decision: Retain scale-prefetch. Scalar-prefetch has identical output and reported resource counts but no performance benefit: only 2/9 faster trials for both full/core APIs, with negative paired median savings. This supports rejecting this candidate, not a statistical-significance or model-quality claim. Equal resources do not prove equal scheduling or identify the critical path. The unchanged baseline's lower time than earlier runs is not a candidate improvement.
